risks.description: If administrative privileges are used for daily tasks (no separate admin account) or admin actions are not properly logged/audited, it becomes hard to prove who performed privileged operations or to limit damage.
risks.possible_consequence: Difficulty in forensic analysis, extended undetected attacker persistence, and inability to attribute or roll back malicious administrative changes.

risks.risk_name: Mobile authentication (Google ID) compromise from password reuse
risks.evidence: user reuses same password across all services; user uses a company-provided Android phone for work tasks
risks.description: Reused credentials that are also used for the Google account on the Android phone allow attackers to abuse Google authentication to access many services, track the device, and access synced data.
risks.possible_consequence: Cross-service takeover including email, cloud drive, app stores; remote tracking or wiping of device; deletion or theft of corporate data.

risks.risk_name: Cloud misconfiguration and improper access control
risks.evidence: company relies on cloud services (e.g., Google Drive) to store and share data
risks.description: Absence of strict procedures for access provisioning, role separation, sharing policies and regular review can lead to overly permissive cloud access and accidental exposure.
risks.possible_consequence: Accidental public exposure of sensitive data, excessive privileges for users, and easier paths for attackers to access corporate information.

risks.risk_name: Credential reuse enables broad account takeover
risks.evidence: user reuses same password across all services
risks.description: Reusing the same password across multiple services means compromise of any one service (personal or third-party) allows an attacker to authenticate to other accounts belonging to the user.
risks.possible_consequence: Unauthorized access to multiple personal and corporate accounts, data theft, identity takeover, and pivot to corporate resources.
risks.analysis_justification: Explicit password reuse materially increases the chance that a breach of any one service will enable takeover of other accounts, including corporate ones; the potential for broad lateral access and data exfiltration makes impact very high.
risks.eits_support: E-ITS notes that using the same passwords on social networks and in the working environment can lead to misuse of IT systems and password revocation, supporting the increased likelihood and impact.

risks.risk_name: Personal password used for work accounts (no separation)
risks.evidence: password is used for work accounts
risks.description: Using a personal or non-dedicated credential for work accounts indicates absence of enforced separation between personal and work authentication credentials or lack of policy enforcement.
risks.possible_consequence: Personal account compromise results in immediate exposure of corporate accounts and data; inability to revoke access selectively.
risks.analysis_justification: Use of a personal credential for work creates a clear path from personal compromise to corporate exposure; while not guaranteed to be exploited, the impact on corporate assets would be significant.

risks.risk_name: Insecure network/configuration when administering systems remotely
risks.evidence: user has administrative privileges on a company-issued computer; E-ITS requires administrative interfaces be protected with secure network protocols (e.g. SSH, TLS)
risks.description: If administrative interfaces or remote management channels are not configured to use secure, encrypted protocols, credentials and management traffic can be intercepted or tampered with.
risks.possible_consequence: Compromise of administrative sessions, unauthorized configuration changes, and escalated access for attackers.
risks.analysis_justification: The presence of administrative access and E-ITS guidance on secure protocols indicate a moderate likelihood that insecure remote admin configurations could be present; impacts of intercepted admin sessions are high.
risks.eits_support: OPS.1.1.2.M6.d explicitly requires protection of administrative account use with secure network protocols and sufficient encryption, supporting this risk assessment.
risks.evaluation_justification: Medium severity with high impact potential; reduce by enforcing secure protocols, network segmentation and encrypted admin channels per E-ITS.

risks.risk_name: Insufficient privacy and app permission management on mobile devices
risks.evidence: user uses a company-provided Android phone for work tasks; SYS.3.2.1.M6 states app access to data and interfaces should be strictly need-based and privacy settings be restrictive
risks.description: If privacy settings are permissive and approval of app permissions is not managed, apps may access more data than necessary for business tasks.
risks.possible_consequence: Unintended data exposure to third parties, leakage of sensitive information, and increased attack surface through inter-app data flows.
risks.analysis_justification: Company mobile use combined with the need for strict app permission management indicates a moderate likelihood of permissive settings being present; resultant privacy/data leakage impacts are assessed as medium.
risks.eits_support: SYS.3.2.1.M6 from E-ITS calls for restrictive privacy settings and need-based app access, directly supporting this control gap.
risks.evaluation_justification: Medium risk to privacy and data controls; reduce by enforcing restrictive app permissions, mobile management and approval workflows per E-ITS.

risks.risk_name: Uncontrolled proliferation of corporate data via collaborative cloud use
risks.evidence: company relies on cloud services such as Google Drive to store and share data; employees regularly access these cloud services to collaborate and manage files
risks.description: Frequent collaborative use of cloud storage without governance leads to multiple copies, uncontrolled sharing links and lack of lifecycle management for sensitive files.
risks.possible_consequence: Data sprawl, inability to locate or delete sensitive data, extended exposure windows and compliance failures.
risks.analysis_justification: Frequent collaborative cloud use makes proliferation and sprawl likely; while this complicates governance and compliance, the direct business impact is assessed as medium.
risks.eits_support: E-ITS guidance on collaborative cloud usage and governance supports the assessment that unmanaged sharing creates governance and compliance risks.
risks.evaluation_justification: Medium governance risk that should be reduced via data lifecycle policies, classification, DLP and collaboration controls per E-ITS.

risks.risk_name: Compromise propagation across corporate systems from a single credential breach
risks.evidence: user reuses the same password across all services; employees regularly access cloud services; user has administrative privileges on a company-issued computer
risks.description: A single compromised credential that is valid across services and on a privileged endpoint can allow attackers to move laterally and escalate privileges across systems.
risks.possible_consequence: Broad and rapid infiltration of corporate networks, widespread data exfiltration, long-term persistence of attackers and severe business impact.
risks.analysis_justification: Combined evidence of universal password reuse, privileged local access, and broad cloud access creates a very high likelihood that a single credential breach could enable lateral movement; potential business and data impacts are very high.
risks.eits_support: E-ITS (OPS.1.1.2.M6 and related sections) emphasise distinct admin credentials, MFA and secure admin practices to prevent exactly this form of cross-system compromise.
risks.evaluation_justification: Very high severity and impact require urgent reduction through unique credentials, MFA, privileged access controls, segmentation and E-ITS-aligned mitigations.
